jenna_customer: Hey team — we're seeing intermittent 401s for SSE streaming to /v1/streams when requests go through our corporate proxy. First observed at 2026-03-16T18:02:14Z. Body includes request_id=req_0a1b2c3d. Using curl from macOS. Can you share exact curl to reproduce and what headers to collect?

sam_support: Sorry you're hitting this, jenna. Can you paste the curl you used? Typical repro we ask for is a minimal curl showing headers + no buffering. Example we use: 

sam_support: ```
# replace $TOKEN and $URL
curl -v -N 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" 
  -D - 
  --http1.1 
  --no-progress-meter 
  "$URL/v1/streams?model=gpt-streaming"
```

sam_support: Please also include `--proxy` and `--proxy-user` flags if you're behind a proxy, and run with `-v` so we can see TLS handshake / CONNECT. If you can, run `--trace-ascii trace.txt` and attach the file.

jenna_customer: Thanks, ran a quick test. Here's what I used (token redacted):

jenna_customer: ```
curl -v -N \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ********" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -D - \ 
  --http1.1 \ 
  --proxy http://corp.proxy.local:8080 \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=gpt-streaming"
```

jenna_customer: Response (truncated):

jenna_customer: ```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 18:02:14 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 72
X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d

{"error":"invalid_token","message":"token missing or invalid","request_id":"req_0a1b2c3d"}
```

lee_infra: Thanks, jenna. Two quick asks: 1) can you run the same curl without the proxy (if possible) to confirm the proxy path is the variable, and 2) run `curl -v --trace-ascii trace.txt` and attach trace.txt so we can see if Authorization is being stripped.

priya_sre: Also please run a header dump to capture exactly what hits our edge. Use: 

priya_sre: ```
curl -v -N -D server-headers.out \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --http1.1 \
  --proxy http://corp.proxy.local:8080 \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=gpt-streaming"
```

priya_sre: Attach server-headers.out and trace.txt. We need request-id + timestamp (you already have req_0a1b2c3d), and whether the proxy is presenting any `Proxy-Authenticate` or modifying Authorization.

jenna_customer: Ran without proxy — no 401, stream opens fine. With proxy it 401s. Attached trace shows the proxy issuing a CONNECT and then later an HTTP/1.1 request where Authorization header is absent. Excerpts: 

jenna_customer: ```
=> CONNECT api.redwood.example:443 HTTP/1.1
=> Host: api.redwood.example
=> Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive

<== HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established

=> GET /v1/streams?model=gpt-streaming HTTP/1.1
=> Accept: text/event-stream
=> User-Agent: curl/8.1.2
=> Host: api.redwood.example
=> 
<== HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
<== X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d
<== Content-Type: application/json
```

jenna_customer: Looks like the `Authorization` header never makes it past the proxy for that particular request path.

lee_infra: That matches a corp proxy policy we saw before — some proxies strip Authorization on cached or streaming endpoints. Two quick workarounds to test: 1) use `Proxy-Authorization` so the proxy satisfies auth to itself (if your proxy requires it), or 2) do a TLS CONNECT and send the Authorization inside the tunnel (curl's CONNECT already does that — but some middleboxes rewrite). To test 1: 

lee_infra: ```
curl -v -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --proxy http://corp.proxy.local:8080 \
  --proxy-user "CORP\\jenna" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=gpt-streaming"
```

priya_sre: If the proxy is the cause we'll need the proxy vendor/time range to escalate. Please collect debug bundle: trace.txt, server-headers.out, the exact curl command you ran, and the timestamp range. You can attach here or upload to the support ticket.

jenna_customer: Tried `--proxy-user` — still 401. Trace shows proxy injecting a `Via:` and `X-Cache` header and dropping Authorization on the GET. Here's server-headers.out: 

jenna_customer: ```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 18:02:14 GMT
Via: 1.1 corp-proxy.local
X-Cache: MISS from corp-proxy
X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"invalid_token","request_id":"req_0a1b2c3d"}
```

sam_support: Ok — thanks, this is solid repro and shows the proxy is the root cause. Two actions: 1) we can document a short-term workaround for you (use an outbound egress rule or a no-proxy for api.redwood.example during streaming), and 2) we'll escalate to enterprise networking. Priya — can you open an escalation with networking with the proxy vendor? I'll attach the debug bundle.

priya_sre: On it. When opening the case include: proxy vendor & version, proxy config (caching rules), example trace + server-headers.out, exact timestamps (2026-03-16T18:02:14Z), and request_id req_0a1b2c3d. Also include Customer's curl and note that Authorization is stripped only on streaming endpoint.

devex_bot: :white_check_mark: Checklist for support bundle created. Please upload trace.txt, server-headers.out, and the curl command to the ticket. Reference: INC-2026-3342.

jenna_customer: Thanks all — I set a temporary no-proxy rule for api.redwood.example and streaming is stable. I'll send the bundle and open the internal ticket for our networking team to coordinate with the proxy vendor. Appreciate the help :heart:

sam_support: Glad that's unblocked. Marking this as resolved on our side for now, but keep the ticket open until networking confirms vendor fix. If you want we can schedule a quick call to review the trace and proposed mitigation.

priya_sre: Adding note: for customers behind aggressive proxies we recommend using Dedicated or Private deployments with explicit network egress controls to avoid header stripping.

jenna_customer: Will do. Attaching bundle shortly.
